evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.limitation: The scenario's input tuple (champion, level, roster composition, item assignment) is defined outside the permitted export -- grep for 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster', 'outgoing_damage_before_death', '2406.2' and '2183.7' over the whole export returned nothing. The computation below is therefore a structural reconstruction: the two golden values plus the wiki-quoted amplifier rule are used to solve for the underlying damage split, and the result is checked for consistency and uniqueness.

sources.source: data/items.json -> id 8020 "Abyssal Mask" -> passives[0] ("Unmake", unique: true) -> branches[0]
sources.quote: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.
sources.reading: Unmake is a debuff on the cursed enemy worth +12% damage taken, RESTRICTED TO MAGIC DAMAGE. 'from all sources' qualifies who may deal that magic damage (any attacker), not which damage types are amplified.
Riot's own tooltip tags the amplified quantity with the magicDamage keyword -- independent confirmation that the 12% is magic-only.

sources.source: data/atoms/items.json -> "8020" -> atom damage.magic (hash 8cd6d6787524e7f7), and data/item-atoms/8020.json -> atom_id "damage.magic"
sources.reading: The cached atomization independently classifies Unmake's 12% under the magic-damage family, not a generic damage family.

sources.source: data/items.json -> id 4005 "Imperial Mandate" -> passives[1] ("Command", unique: true) -> branches[0]
sources.quote: {{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
sources.reading: Vulnerable is a +7% damage-taken debuff that IS type-agnostic ('the damage they take from all sources'). Re-application extends duration only -- it explicitly does not stack in magnitude.

sources.source: docs/math-foundations.md section 2.1 (the 100/(100+R) identity) and the exactness table (lines 455-480)
sources.quote: post = raw * m(R)  <=>  raw = post * (1 + R/100) = post * EHP_multiplier(R)
sources.reading: Mitigation is a per-damage-type linear scaling, so a damage-taken amplifier commutes with mitigation: applying the amp pre- or post-mitigation gives the same total. The reconstruction below can therefore work in post-mitigation, pre-amplification units without loss. math-foundations.md contains no rule that would let a magic-only amplifier touch physical or true damage.

correct_model.statement: Let D_nm and D_m be breakdown[0]'s post-mitigation, pre-amplification outgoing damage in non-magic (physical + true) and magic respectively. Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable (+7%, all types, S2) applies to both; Abyssal Mask's Unmake (+12%, magic only, S1/S1b/S1c) applies to D_m alone.
correct_model.buggy_alternative_that_reproduces_the_ol: outgoing_damage_before_death = 1.07 * 1.12 * (D_nm + D_m)   [Unmake's 12% leaked onto non-magic damage]

independent_computation.step_2_which_amp_moved: 222.5 is 12%-sized, not 7%-sized. If the change had been the removal/addition of Imperial Mandate's 7% Vulnerable, the amplified base would have to be 222.5 / 0.07 = 3178.57 -- larger than the entire new total of 2183.7, which is impossible. So the leaf moved by a 12% amplifier being withdrawn from a sub-portion of the damage: 222.5 / 0.12 = 1854.17 of post-Vulnerable output, i.e. 1854.17 / 2183.7 = 84.9% of the new total. That 12% is Abyssal Mask's Unmake (S1) -- the only 12% amplifier in the scenario.
independent_computation.conclusion: The pair (old, new) is exactly the pair (Unmake applied to all damage, Unmake applied to magic damage only) for an attacker dealing ~86% non-magic / ~14% magic. The new value is the one that obeys the wiki text.
independent_computation.robustness_to_the_stacking_convention: If the engine composes damage-taken amps additively (magic x 1.19, non-magic x 1.07) rather than multiplicatively, the same two golden values solve to D_nm = 1854.17, D_m = 167.85, and the old value is again reproduced by 1.19 * (D_nm + D_m) -- i.e. by letting the curse amplify non-magic damage. The verdict does not depend on the additive-vs-multiplicative choice.

alternatives_considered.hypothesis: The old value was correct and the new one under-applies (Unmake legitimately amplifies physical/true damage).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Directly contradicted by S1 ('12% increased magic damage'), S1b (Riot tooltip tags magicDamage) and S1c (atomized as damage.magic). Nothing in the cached data licenses a magic-only amplifier touching other damage types.

alternatives_considered.hypothesis: The old value stacked Unmake from two roster holders (1 + 0.12 + 0.12 = 1.24) and the fix made it unique; the attacker would then be ~95% magic (D_m = 1732.87, D_nm = 100.03).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Arithmetically self-consistent too, but (a) it makes the pairing with Imperial Mandate pointless -- the scenario deliberately combines a type-agnostic amp ('all sources', S2) with a type-restricted one, which only discriminates on an attacker with a meaningful non-magic majority; (b) the scenario name is singular ('abyssal_curse'); (c) Unmake is flagged unique: true in the cached item record. NOTE: this alternative ALSO makes the new (lower) value the correct one -- under it the old value double-counted a non-stacking curse. Every reading of the cached text that can produce a 222.5 delta makes the OLD value an over-application of Unmake.

alternatives_considered.hypothesis: Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable was double-applied (7% twice) and the fix collapsed it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: S2 states subsequent immobilizes extend the duration, not the magnitude; and numerically a 7%-sized change cannot produce a 222.5 delta on a 2183.7 total (see step_2).

caveat: Because the scenario's input tuple lives outside the permitted evidence tree, D_nm and D_m were solved for rather than read. The verdict rests on (i) the wiki text being unambiguous that Unmake amplifies magic damage only while Vulnerable amplifies all damage, and (ii) the delta being uniquely explicable as a 12% amplifier withdrawn from 84.9% of the output -- both of which point the same way regardless of which of the two candidate root causes is the real one.
